sources.title: Burkina Faso Key Message Update September 2026–January 2027: Agropastoral production prospects negatively affected by El Niño conditions
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed 2026 rainy-season conditions and food-security projections through January 2027.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET key-message monitoring and food-security projections.
sources.limitations: High-level regional summary; it does not attribute violence to climate.

sources.title: Burkina Faso: Fourth Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, Financing Assurances Review, and Request for an Arrangement Under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed context through late 2025; reform program runs through September 2027.
sources.methodology: IMF staff review of the ECF arrangement and RSF request, including macroeconomic analysis and policy discussions.
sources.limitations: The farmer-herder/conflict statement is a national-level narrative, not a localized causal estimate; reform measures are commitments, not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Humanitarian Action for Children 2026: Burkina Faso
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 displacement and service data, 2026 humanitarian needs and planned response.
sources.methodology: Appeal aligns with the 2026 HNRP and participatory JIAF 2.0 analysis.
sources.limitations: Reports needs estimates and planned activities, not outcomes; names unchanged.

sources.title: National bulletins vs the ASAP trigger — September 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, Centre for Humanitarian Data
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 rainy season, with comparison to the JRC ASAP trigger record since 2001.
sources.methodology: OCHA compares JRC ASAP alerts with summaries of ANAM bulletins and a July 2026 SAP-GTP field mission.
sources.limitations: Underlying bulletins and mission findings are summarized, not republished; station and historical coverage are weak in the action area.

sources.title: Quatre Plans d’Action Anticipatoire pour agir avant la sécheresse au Burkina Faso [Four Anticipatory Action Plans to act before drought in Burkina Faso]
sources.temporal_coverage: Summary of four anticipatory-action plans covering 2025–2027.
sources.methodology: Oxfam summarizes four community-developed anticipatory-action plans and links their detailed PDFs.
sources.limitations: Only the summary page was accessible; it documents planned actions, not implementation or results.

claims.locator: Key Messages, bullets on Karo Peli and agropastoral production
claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET reports that late and uneven rains and prolonged August–September dry spells reduced maize yields, pasture growth and water-catchment replenishment, especially in northern Burkina Faso.
claims.limitations: This is a 2026 seasonal assessment and does not establish anthropogenic climate attribution.

claims.locator: Key Messages, first bullet on Karo Peli Province
claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET reported Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes in Karo Peli in September and projected them through January 2027; poor rainfall and dry spells constrain harvests, while low incomes limit food purchases and food aid remains a key support.
claims.scenario: FEWS NET's September 2026–January 2027 outlook; no named climate scenario is specified.
claims.limitations: The page gives a high-level projection and does not identify which households received assistance.

claims.locator: Key Messages, bullet on insecurity and market access
claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET identifies insecurity and armed-group attacks as the main constraint on household food and income access in the north and east; attacks disrupt market supply and displaced 11,316 people in August 2026.
claims.limitations: The update names insecurity as the access constraint but does not connect it causally to the reported rainfall conditions.

claims.paraphrase: IMF staff state that droughts and floods stoke terrorism by fomenting conflicts, especially between herders and farmers.
claims.limitations: This is a high-level staff narrative with no subnational case, causal estimation, or confidence interval in the cited passage.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report explicitly states that droughts and floods fuel terrorism through farmer-herder conflict (printed p. 5, paragraph 2).

claims.locator: Printed p. 2, opening RSF request paragraph
claims.paraphrase: The IMF-supported 2026–2027 Resilience and Sustainability Facility reform package includes disaster-risk finance, climate-resilient public infrastructure investment, resilient utilities, and climate-finance mobilization.
claims.limitations: The source documents a reform package and financing arrangement, not completed measures or resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1 (cover) and PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), opening humanitarian-needs text
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF estimates 4.5 million people, including 2.9 million children, need 2026 assistance; it names climate shocks, displacement and food insecurity as joint drivers of child needs among displaced people, returnees and hosts.
institutions: Burkina Faso Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan
claims.limitations: National estimates do not show that climate caused displacement.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF lists climate shocks, displacement and food insecurity as joint drivers of child humanitarian need (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1).

claims.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), nutrition and water-service needs
claims.paraphrase: Highest nutrition severity is reported in Liptako, Soum, Koulsé, Goulmou, Tapoa, Sirba, Yaadga, Bankui and Sourou. Displacement strains fragile health systems; women and girls face water-collection protection risks.
claims.limitations: The source does not attribute regional severity to climate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Displacement increases demand on safe-water and health services; women and girls face collection-related protection risks (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1).

claims.locator: Sections 1–2 and 4; 2026 trigger status and monitoring-gap assessment
claims.paraphrase: OCHA reports that the CERF drought framework covers Loroum, Oudalan, Séno and Yagha; its observational trigger was not activated in July–August, while national bulletins lacked province-level values and historical records needed for a formal alternate trigger.
claims.limitations: September trigger dekads were still pending when OCHA published the page on 10 September 2026.

claims.locator: Section 2, AOI-relevant rainfall-stations table, Dori row
claims.paraphrase: OCHA's comparison reports late onset, rainfall 10–50% below normal, 7–10-day dry spells and low dam levels across the four framework provinces; at Dori in Séno, rainfall was 321 mm by 31 August versus a 414 mm 1991–2020 normal.
claims.limitations: Dori was the only listed station within the four-province area; there were no listed gauges for Loroum, Oudalan or Yagha.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs 2–3, locations and community-planning process
claims.paraphrase: Oxfam and partners report four 2025–2027 drought anticipatory-action plans for Santéna (Boussouma), Damesma (Kaya), Somiaga (Ouahigouya) and Zougoungou (Gomponsom), developed with community vulnerability-and-capacity assessments and triggers using ANAM forecasts, PRESASS analysis and community early-warning observations.
claims.limitations: The summary page describes plan design; it does not verify implementation, reach or outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The four plans envisage adapted agricultural inputs, food assistance, hygiene and dignity kits, heat-protection kits and income-generating support for vulnerable households; Oxfam says several thousand people are targeted.
claims.limitations: These are intended actions and target reach; the source reports no delivery or measured resilience gains.

search_audit.query: Burkina Faso 2026 subnational climate drought food vulnerability regional report government UN
search_audit.outcome: Found and read FEWS NET September 2026 update and OCHA September 2026 drought bulletin comparison with named provinces and station-level rainfall; local coverage remains uneven.

search_audit.query: Burkina Faso drought farmer herder conflict climate security primary source 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Found an explicit IMF staff statement that drought and flood pressures can fuel terrorism through farmer-herder conflict; it is national-level and not empirically localized in the cited passage.

search_audit.query: Burkina Faso conflict insecurity displacement limits climate adaptation access pastoralism local report 2026
search_audit.outcome: FEWS NET reports insecurity restricting household food and income access and driving displacement; UNICEF documents displacement-related pressure on health and water services. No accessed source linked this reverse pathway specifically to local climate-adaptation outcomes.

search_audit.query: Burkina Faso drought anticipatory action resilience capacity early warning 2026 OCHA UNICEF Oxfam
search_audit.outcome: Found a four-province CERF early-warning framework, UNICEF planned anticipatory action, and four Oxfam-supported community plans; linked Oxfam plan PDFs were not accessible and the inspected sources do not establish delivery outcomes.

gaps: OCHA reports that rainfall-station coverage is thinnest inside the Loroum–Oudalan–Séno–Yagha anticipatory-action area; Dori was the only listed station inside it.
The public Oxfam page summarizes four community plans, but the linked detailed plan PDFs could not be inspected, so local targeting, triggers and delivery performance remain unverified.
The accessed IMF climate-security statement is national-level; no new localized causal study linking specific rainfall or flood events to farmer-herder violence was accessed.
The searched sources document insecurity-related access and displacement, but do not quantify how insecurity changed climate adaptation delivery or climate-resilience outcomes in named places.
